Monarch on Butterfly Milkweed

Monarch Among Prairie Flowers

Open Wings on Butterfly Milkweed

Danaus plexippus

The Monarch is one of the most recognizable North American butterflies, with broad orange wings, bold black veins, and black borders marked with white spots. These photos show the butterfly visiting Butterfly Milkweed, nectaring among tall prairie flowers, approaching purple thistle in flight, and as a striped caterpillar on milkweed.

For identification details, life-cycle notes, host plant information, and comparison with similar orange-and-black butterflies, see Danaus plexippus in the Field Notes section. For photographic observations and visual context, see Photographic Sequence in the Field Notes section. The Monarch is also shown visiting Butterfly Milkweed on the plant Field Notes page.
